# Elektrificeringsbølgen giver muligheder i small- og midcap-aktier

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-10-08  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

This Danish EuroInvestor Millionærklubben episode focuses on electrification as a multi-decade megatrend. Guest Thomas Tang of Medium Invest argues that grid expansion is the bottleneck and the best opportunity, and that grid contractors are cheap. He names Friedrich Vorwerk, NYAB and the newly listed Linjemontage as holdings. The macro backdrop is cautious: rising US yields, oil above $102, Middle East tensions and European debt worries. There is also news on ALK, Zealand Pharma, Bavarian Nordic and Samsung, and AI demand is described as strong.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 VH2 — Friedrich Vorwerk | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 85%

Guest (Thomas Tang, Medium Invest) owns it: the biggest grid-build exposure, P/E ~11, EV/EBIT ~7, insider buying; 'ticked all the boxes'

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Most of its revenue comes from German grid expansion, and Germany has the largest investment plans. Budgets set by regulators give visibility into growth for many years. The valuation is very low after a 25% YTD fall. The fund values stocks on a five-year horizon. Risk: Germany may move to more overhead lines instead of underground cables. He would trim after a ~50% rise and likely sell after a 100% rise.

#### Sell Triggers

- stock rises 50-100% (trim/sell)
- Germany shifts from underground to overhead cables
- a cheaper alternative investment appears
- grid investment budgets are cut

> *"Så den tækkede alle boksene hos os."*

---

### 🟢 NYAB — Nyab | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Guest holds it as a top candidate for grid expansion: low valuation and high expected revenue/earnings growth; bought 3-4 months ago, up 27% YTD

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Held as part of a three-name grid-contractor basket. Grid demand is described as structural rather than boom-bust, because aging grids need replacing. The guest admits contractors have weak moats, but the whole sector is lifted by a shortage of capacity. If NYAB rises 50% relative to its peers, he may move the money into the other two names.

#### Sell Triggers

- stock rises ~50% relative to peers (rebalance)
- grid investment slows
- new competitors erode margins

> *"Det gjorde vi for 3-4 måneder siden, så den har vi tajmet rigtig godt."*

---

### 🟢 LMGAB — Linjemontage | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest bought it in the September IPO at SEK 46; high exposure to grid expansion in several countries and low valuation

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. He describes it as the same thesis as NYAB and Vorwerk: high grid exposure, low valuation and many strong years ahead. Peers make it easy to value. It is a recent IPO, which the guest says is an exception to his rule. The three names are held as a basket to spread single-stock risk.

#### Sell Triggers

- stock rises ~50% relative to peers (rebalance)
- grid capex slows
- execution problems after IPO

> *"Høj eksponering mod udbygningen af elnettet i forskellige lande, lav prissætning."*

---

### 🟡 MCB — McBride | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest sees the hit from oil-driven input costs as temporary; keeps holding and would buy more if the stock falls too much

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion. Soap demand is stable through the economic cycle. Higher oil-linked input costs hurt earnings for a while, because price increases reach customers with a delay. Costs can be fully passed on, so the hit is judged temporary rather than permanent. Other parts of the business are going well.

#### Sell Triggers

- cost pass-through fails
- earnings damage proves permanent

> *"McBride vurderer vi, at det er en midlertidig påvirkning, så holder vi fast, køber op, hvis den falder for meget på det."*

---
